title: Child Safety Seat Tether Anchor Removal and Installation
introduction: The child safety seat tether anchor sits beneath the rear seat cushion. I think of the cushion as the access lid: release its locking tabs before reaching for the anchor hardware. The drawings guide you through that access, and the final belt-routing check matters just as much as putting the cushion back.

items.name: Arrange access
items.detail: Move both front seats fully forward before removing the rear cushion. Have a torque wrench suitable for the anchor-retainer specification.

items.name: Protect the cushion tabs
items.detail: Press the cushion locking tabs inward to release them from the floor before lifting the cushion. Lifting without releasing them can damage the tabs.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Before beginning service, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during service, causing personal injury or death. Once seat access is arranged, remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to use the applicable protection may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show a left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicle; the procedure is similar for right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles.
edits.why: Steering position changes the illustrated configuration, so use the component locations as your guide.

edits.text: NOTE: The right-hand (RH) anchor is illustrated; the left-hand (LH) anchor is serviced in a similar way.
edits.why: The side qualifier identifies which anchor the drawing shows without limiting the procedure to that side.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting installation; they also contain details needed for refitting.
edits.why: The tightening specification appears beside removal, but applies when securing the anchor during installation.

edits.text:
Move both front seats fully forward. At the front of the rear seat cushion, press the locking tabs inward to release the cushion from the floor. Lift and release the cushion, then remove it. The tabs must be pressed in before lifting, or they can be damaged.
Refer to: [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The cushion conceals the anchor mounting area. I use the cushion drawing to locate the releases: these are latches to disengage, not attachments to overcome by pulling harder.

edits.text: Remove the retainers, then remove the child safety seat tether anchor shown in the illustration. During installation, tighten the retainers to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).
edits.why: The blue highlight identifies the anchor and the magenta highlights identify its retainers. The torque is the installation tightening specification, not a removal setting.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: refit the anchor and secure its retainers to the specified torque, then reinstall the rear seat cushion. During cushion installation, make sure the seatbelt webbing is not twisted and that the seatbelts and buckles remain accessible to the occupant.
edits.why: A fitted cushion can conceal trapped belt hardware. Finish by checking belt routing and buckle access rather than judging completion by the cushion's appearance alone.
